title: SDK snapstart: 15min rituals & edge checks (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience: quick set of minimal, repeatable steps engineers can run in 15 minutes when integrating Redwood SDK into a new service or demo. Focus: reduce time-to-first-successful-request, capture lightweight telemetry, surface three high-probability failure modes, and provide quick mitigations. Intended for: backend engineers, full-stack devs running a prototype, SDK oncall, SEs running demos.

Goals (high level):
- First call: success within 15 minutes (auth + generate + parse).
- Observable: one-line telemetry check and one trace to inspect.
- Fail-fast: catch common auth/network/compatibility errors and give 1-line fixes.
- Repro: local mode that mimics dedicated environment for smoke runs.

Constraints / assumptions:
- User has a GitHub account and can run docker or python.
- Minimal dependencies: python 3.10+, curl, docker (optional).
- We do not create a full sample app here — this is a pocket ritual for rapid verification.

Quick checklist (15 minute path):
1) Prep (2 min)
- Ensure API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXXXX
- Pick a tiny test model: rwd-small-1 (or 'open-chat-mini' if not available)
- Repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk/examples/minimal

2) Install & run (5 min)
- Python quick install:
  - python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  - pip install -r requirements-minimal.txt
- Example run (node/python):
  - python quick_start_invoke.py --model rwd-small-1 --prompt "Say hi"
- Expected output: json-ish streaming or single response with "Hello" or similar.

3) Telemetry sanity check (2 min)
- One-line event: curl -X GET \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health
- Verify: status 200 + {"uptime" : "..."} and fields: request_count, avg_latency_ms.
- If missing: validate network (VPN / corp proxies) and key scope (check org/token permissions).

4) Failure playlist & triage (4 min)
- Auth 401/403: "invalid_token" or "insufficient_scope". Quick fix: regenerate key, ensure env var set, ensure key not scoped to only embeddings.
- Model mismatch 422: "model not found" or incompatible variant. Quick fix: try fallback model rwd-small-1 or pinned alias rwd-small-1-v1.
- Network timeout / handshake: typically corp proxy or missing SNI. Quick fix: curl the health endpoint; set NO_PROXY for local. If docker, add --network=host for initial smoke.

5) Rollback / local-mode fallback (2 min)
- Local dev shim: small docker image runs a stub server that mirrors successful responses for UX flows. Command: docker compose -f docker/local-shim.yml up --build -d
- Swap endpoint: export REDWOOD_API_HOST=http://localhost:8080 && re-run sample.

6) Quicknotes for SE/demo (1 min)
- Keep a short script: 3 lines (auth, run, status).
- If streaming demo: use --stream flag and confirm truncation handling.

Detailed snippets (paste-ready)
- minimal python invocation (quick_start_invoke.py):
  import os, requests
  API = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
  HOST = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_HOST','https://api.redwood-inference.internal')
  r = requests.post(f"{HOST}/v1/generate", json={"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"hi"}, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {API}"}, timeout=8)
  print(r.status_code, r.text)

- local shim docker-compose fragment (docker/local-shim.yml)
  version: '3.7'
  services:
    shim:
      image: redwood/shim-stub:latest
      ports:
        - "8080:8080"
      environment:
        - RESPONSE_TEXT="{\"status\":\"ok\",\"text\":\"shim reply\"}"

Operator heuristics and subtle tips
- Telemetry: prefer short-lived trace ID printed on the sample run so SEs can open Console -> traces -> trace-id quickly. Add env var SAMPLE_TRACE_ID for runs to correlate.
- Latency noise: when benchmarking, warm the model by sending 2 short requests before measuring.
- Token billing: demo with 'max_tokens' small (16) and log token usage. Always include a 'cost estimate' line in demo artifact.
- Avoid streaming for first-run: streaming introduces client-side parsing complexity; make first success non-streaming.

Open questions / TODO (for this draft)
- Do we include a tiny Node + curl alternate path in the same doc or split? (lean to single page, two tabs)
- Should the local-shim be published to ghcr with a stable tag for 'oncall quickstart'? (priority: yes)
- Add a small checklist card in Console UI tied to first-run telemetry? (design sync needed with Console team)

Links / references
- Quickstart example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples/minimal
- Telemetry guide PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/212

Notes to self (scratch)
- Keep language extremely prescriptive: copy/paste commands, minimal cognitive load.
- Add a 1-page printable "SE quick card" PDF for laptop demos.
- Consider a 30s recording embed showing the three steps (export key, run, check health) — useful for support triage.

Last-minute checklist before publishing:
- [ ] confirm example API endpoint hostnames (internal vs public)
- [ ] add node/curl snippets (short)
- [ ] merge shim image PR and add stable tag

End of draft.
